eligibility.quote: it appears that the formula got copied wrong from Wikipedia, as applying the absolute-value function in the place it was at prevented detection of the long-way-around case.

loudness.quote: Note how the interpolated angle has value 0.285: it's taking the long way around, with the interpolation going through 0 instead of Pi/-Pi radians.

resolution.quote: PR is merged, so I'm closing this

notes: Independent check agrees with ineligible/internal (E2 step 2). Verified this session: (1) issue #1478 'Floating joint interpolation takes the long way around' by werner291; body contains the reproducer calling 'fjm.interpolate(jv1, jv2, 0.5, intp);' and the printed values AA 2.07858 about +z (0,0,1), BB 2.64902 about -z (-0,-0,-1), CC 0.285223 about -z — matching the spec's E4 evidence verbatim; (2) PR #1479 'Fixed fabs() use in quaternion interpolation' body quote verified verbatim; merged 2022-08-09 as 59e69bbead595cf2a8e2c2b1f4faa5d847d57e5a; (3) diff verified in moveit_core/robot_model/src/floating_joint_model.cpp: removed 'double dq = fabs(from[3] * to[3] + from[4] * to[4] + from[5] * to[5] + from[6] * to[6]);' and 'if (dq < 0)  // Take care of long angle case see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slerp', added 'Eigen::Quaterniond q = q1.slerp(t, q2);' — exactly as the spec describes; PR files are floating_joint_model.cpp and test/test.cpp only; (4) randomized interpolation unit test verified in the test diff ('TEST(FloatingJointTest, interpolation_test)' using 'random_numbers::RandomNumberGenerator rng' and 'fjm.getVariableRandomPositions(rng, jv1, bounds);'); (5) closing comment by henningkayser verified verbatim ('PR is merged, so I'm closing this'); (6) the component-order note verified in the diff: '+    // Note the ordering: Eigen takes w first!' — handled inside the same function, not across a unit boundary. Wrong arithmetic inside moveit_core's FloatingJointModel::interpolate; any correct caller receives the same wrong interpolation, and the reproducer calls the library function directly (no composition of two units), so E2 stops at step 2 and E3 correctly fails. Loudness/resolution null is schema-correct for an ineligible case.
